title: SRE weekly sketchpad — operational highlights & handoff (Nov 21 2027)
content:
Purpose: quick sync for the week ending 2027-11-21 — lightweight notes for on-call handoff, incident sketches, SLO snapshot, and next-step action items. Treat this as a mutable sketchpad; detailed postmortems will land in JIRA for sev2+ incidents.

TL;DR:
- Three notable events this week: a transient KV cache regression affecting hosted-api p99 (short outage window), an autoscaler misconfiguration that led to noisy evictions on a dedicated GPU pool, and a degraded tracing ingest pipeline causing gaps in distributed traces. No customer data exposure. Error budget impact contained to hosted-api route for a 6-hour window.
- SLOs: hosted-api availability dipped but recovered; error budget remaining for hosted-api: 76%. Keep an eye on p99 tokens for long-tail prompts.
- On-call: handoff notes below include immediate mitigations and who owns follow-ups.

Incidents (sketch summaries):
1) Incident SRE-4321 — KV prefix cache regression (2027-11-18 04:12 UTC)
   - What happened: a deployment (platform PR #2156) changed TTL logic for prefix cache keys; under a particular request pattern we saw excessive cache churn and thundering rehydrations. Caused p99 latency spikes for hosted-api text-generation route.
   - Detection: alerted by p99-latency-alert (threshold 1.2s) and increased CPU on inference frontends.
   - Impact: 6h window of elevated p99 (median ok). Some requests retried by clients; few support tickets about slow responses, no 5xx surge.
   - Mitigation: rolled back PR, bumped cache TTL to conservative defaults, added a circuit-breaker to avoid synchronous rehydration.
   - Next: full postmortem in JIRA (JIRA-SRE-4321). Add a unit-level test for TTL behavior in prefix-cache lib.

2) Incident SRE-4387 — Dedicated pool autoscale oscillations (2027-11-19 13:40 UTC)
   - What happened: new autoscaler rule included a low smoothing window + aggressive scale-down; during a burst of short requests the controller interpreted transient drop in queue-length as sustained, scaled-down nodes, then scaled back up — causing pod evictions and scheduling pressure. Some dedicated customers saw increased tail latency and timeouts on long streaming sessions.
   - Detection: internal alert: node-evictions > 20/min. Pager triggered for on-call infra.
   - Mitigation: temporarily set scale-down disabled for critical GPU pools, reverted the smoothing window to prior setting.
   - Next: work with platform-autoscale team to add canarying for autoscaler param changes and a safety floor for minimum nodes for pools with streaming sessions. Owner: Mateo Ruiz. ETA: 2027-11-28.

3) Tracing ingest gaps (2027-11-20 morning)
   - What happened: trace-forwarder experienced backpressure when tracing storage rotated unexpectedly; sampling metadata lost for a subset of traces, resulting in gaps in cross-service traces for ~3 hours.
   - Detection: trace-coverage metric dropped and alerting dashboard showed missing spans.
   - Mitigation: increased buffer capacity and applied a hotfix to the forwarder to gracefully reject vs block.
   - Next: write a runbook step for forwarder rotation, and schedule a maintenance test. Owner: Priya Nair. ETA: 2027-12-02.

SLO snapshot (as of 2027-11-21 08:00 UTC):
- hosted-api availability (window 30d): 99.92% (target 99.99%). Error budget remaining: 76%
- embeddings-api availability: 99.995% (target 99.95%) — healthy
- p99 generation latency (hosted-api): 0.82s baseline, spike to 1.6s during SRE-4321
- Dedicated pool tail latency (90d): steady but watch for post-oscillation spikes
- Alert noise: medium — two noisy alerts (autoscaler and cache) triggered duplicate pages; refine alert routing

Operational notes & diagnostics highlights:
- KV cache: add a small synthetic load test that mimics large numbers of short prefix invalidations; run as part of the PR check for prefix-cache changes.
- Autoscale: missing safety floor is recurring theme; propose a minimal-nodes policy per pool in the next platform-ops RFC.
- Traces: ensure trace sampling metadata is persisted separately from transient buffers so rotation doesn't drop context.
- Observability: tracing gaps highlighted that some dashboards lack fallback visualizations; small UX ask for dashboard team to show last-known-state overlays.

On-call handoff (to next-week oncall: Liam O'Connor) — immediate points:
- Keep autoscale scale-down disabled on GPU-critical pools until platform-autoscale implements safety floor (owner: Mateo Ruiz).
- If hosted-api p99 > 1.0s again: check prefix-cache rehydration rate (metric: prefix_cache.rehydrations_per_min) and correlation with platform deployments. Quick mitigation: roll back recent prefix-cache library changes.
- Tracing gaps: if trace-coverage drops again, flip forwarder to reject-on-full mode (playbook step in Confluence link) and open emergency ticket with storage team.
- Customer escalations: CS tickets #4729, #4731 reference timeouts for streaming sessions — route to Dedicated support and mention autoscale mitigation.

Action items (owner — brief status — due):
- Mateo Ruiz — Implement safety-floor config & canarying for autoscaler param changes — in_progress — due 2027-11-28
- Priya Nair — Add rotation-safe behavior and a runbook entry for trace-forwarder — in_progress — due 2027-12-02
- Ava Chen — Add prefix-cache TTL unit tests and a synthetic workload in CI — todo — due 2027-11-30
- Zoe Park — Review alerting routing for cache and autoscale alerts to reduce duplicate pages — todo — due 2027-11-26

Open questions / discussion items:
- Should safety floors be per-customer-pool or global-per-tier? Tradeoffs: flexibility vs operational simplicity.
- For prefix-cache: do we move to eventual-consistency by default (defer synchronous rehydration) or keep strong sync with smarter backoff?
- Do we want a small permanent canary cluster for infra changes (autoscaler, cache libs) that accepts ~1% of traffic for 24h? Pros/cons and cost estimates needed.

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This doc is intentionally lightweight — captures what oncall should know right now. Postmortems will contain timelines and RCA when completed.
- Slack threads: #sre-kv-cache, #platform-autoscale. See linked_artifacts for JIRA items + PR.

Appendix: quick links
- JIRA-SRE-4321 (kv cache)
- JIRA-SRE-4387 (autoscale oscillation)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2156
- Confluence runbook: /sre/runbooks/kv-cache-resilience

End of sketchpad.
